'''''Carex pseudocyperus''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Cyperaceae|sedge family]] known by the common name '''cyperus sedge'''<ref name=BSBI>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> or '''hop sedge'''.<ref name=Fitter>{{cite book|last1=Fitter|first1=Richard |authorlink1=R. S. R. Fitter |last2=Fitter |first2=Alastair |authorlink2=Alastair Fitter |last3=Farrer |first3=Ann|title=Collins Guide to the Grasses, Sedges, Rushes and Ferns of Britain and Northern Europe|place=London|date=1984|page=142|isbn=0-00-219136-9}}</ref> It grows in marshes, swamps, and the margins of ponds, rivers and canals. The stems can be up to {{convert|90|cm}} with one male spike and 3 to 5 pendulous female spikes, and bright yellow-green leaves to {{convert|1.2|m}}.<ref name=Fitter /><ref name=Stace>{{cite book |last=Stace |first=Clive A. |authorlink=Clive A. Stace |year=2010 |title=New flora of the British isles |url=https://archive.org/details/newflorabritishi00stac |url-access=limited |edition=Third |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge, U.K. |page=[https://archive.org/details/newflorabritishi00stac/page/n1000 965] |isbn=9780521707725 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora |url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/index.php?q=plant/Carex-pseudocyperus}}</ref>
